cohort: 65,173 women who delivered singleton babies at or after 28 weeks gestation in 25 hospitals in 9 provinces in northern China
finding: Male fetal gender was associated with an increased incidence of preterm delivery, gestational diabetes mellitus, fetal macrosomia, lower Apgar score, perinatal death, placenta previa, increased cesarean section delivery, and operative delivery, while female fetuses were associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia at an advanced gestational age, fetal growth restriction, malpresentation, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Male fetal gender was associated with increased cesarean section delivery and operative delivery.
